Double deep Q-network based multi-objective optimization for ﬂexible job 
shop scheduling problem with heterogeneous automatic guided vehicles
Rensheng Chen
, Bin Wu
∗
School of Economics and Management, Nanjing Tech University, Nanjing, 211816, China
a r t i c l e  i n f o
Keywords:
Flexible job shop scheduling problem
Heterogeneous automatic guided vehicles
Double deep Q-network
Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II
Local search
 
a b s t r a c t
In highly ﬂexible automated manufacturing workshops, jobs need to be transported frequently between ma-
chines, so the limitations of transportation resources are receiving increasing attention. This paper investigates 
the ﬂexible job shop scheduling problem with heterogeneous automatic guided vehicles (AGVs). A double deep Q-
network (double DQN) based non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II is proposed to minimize the makespan 
and total energy consumption. Firstly, an initialization strategy based on multiple heuristic methods is designed 
for better performance. Secondly, critical paths and blocks within the problem are identiﬁed using a disjunc-
tive graph, from which six problem-driven local search operators are developed. Thirdly, double DQN is used 
to recommend the optimal local search operator. 13 features are selected to describe the current state of an 
individual, and the proposed operators are employed as actions. The eﬀectiveness of the proposed algorithm 
is evaluated by comparing with four other advanced algorithms. Finally, a real world case is used to analyze 
the greater potential of heterogeneous AGVs compared with homogeneous AGVs in optimizing two objective
values.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: With the rise of Industry 4.0, the manufacturing industry, as the core of the industry and the pillar of the national economy, is facing many key challenges of transformation and upgrading, among which the flex- ible job shop scheduling problem (FJSP) is one of the important prob- lems to be solved urgently ( Dauzère-Pérès et al. , 2024 ; Gao et al. , 2019 ). The complexity of this problem is further exacerbated in the context of intelligent manufacturing, especially with the rapid development and widespread application of Automatic Guided Vehicles (AGVs) technol- ogy ( Tan et al. , 2021 ). The flexible job scheduling problem with AGV (FJSP-A) has made job transportation a crucial element of scheduling decisions, enhancing both the flexibility and automation of workshops while simultaneously increasing the complexity of interactions between jobs, machines, and AGVs ( Berterottière et al. , 2024 ). In particular, as production environments and task requirements evolve, intelligent fac- tories are increasingly deploying heterogeneous AGVs fleet. Heteroge- neous AGVs have their own advantages and disadvantages in terms of battery capacity, transportation speed, energy consumption and charg- ing speed. How to reasonably allocate heterogeneous AGVs according to task demand and scheduling situation to reduce schedule delay and ∗ Corresponding author. E-mail address: wubin@njtech.edu.cn (B. Wu). resource waste has become a key focus for managing heterogeneous AGVs fleet ( Singh et al. , 2022 ). Therefore, the flexible job shop schedul- ing problem with heterogeneous AGVs (FJSP-HA) is of great significance for meeting production requirements while minimizing costs and im- proving work efficiency. The FJSP-A problem not only demands the optimization of produc- tion operations within job shops but also necessitates the coordination of the AGV transportation system to ensure the smooth and efficient func- tioning of the entire production process ( Pan et al. , 2022 ; Yao et al. , 2024b ). While, several literatures have focused on the optimization of AGV paths and tasks in FJSP-A problem ( Amirteimoori et al. , 2023 ; Gao et al. , 2024 ), but there is still a lack of research on the FJSP-A problem with limited battery capacity. The task execution of AGVs is often inter- rupted by charging constraints, resulting in production schedule delays, which is further complicated when heterogeneous AGVs are used ( Li & Huang , 2024 ). Due to the unique performance parameters of heteroge- neous AGVs, there are differences in the selection of AGVs for differ- ent transportation tasks and scheduling time nodes ( Li et al. , 2022a ). For example, underride AGV has the characteristics of lightweight, high flexibility and high speed, which can complete transportation tasks in a short time, and is suitable for jobs that need to be delivered quickly https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2025.128992 Received 13 May 2025; Received in revised form 4 July 2025; Accepted 9 July 2025 Expert Systems With Applications 296 (2026) 128992 Available online 23 July 2025 0957-4174/© 2025 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies. R. Chen et al. in FJSP-A problem. However, early arrival is of limited benefit for jobs that the subsequent machine is still occupied. Additionally, since their small size limits the battery capacity, over-reliance on underride AGVs will lead to frequent recharging, which will reduce the overall schedul- ing efficiency ( Song et al. , 2024 ). In contrast, the towing AGV, although slower due to lack of flexibility, has longer battery life due to its larger battery capacity. However, its low transport speed may lead to the de- lay of some transport tasks, causing the waiting of processing machines and the delay of the completion time of operations ( Xing et al. , 2023 ). sections.heading: Literature
sections.text: review 2.1. Flexible job shop scheduling problem with AGVs The widespread adoption of AGV in modern manufacturing has spurred global research and exploration into integrated solutions for production and transportation scheduling. Fontes et al. ( 2024 ) proposed a multi-population biased random-key genetic algorithm to study the joint scheduling of variable-speed machines and AGVs. Barak et al. ( 2021 ) developed a mathematical model for the FJSP-A problem, in- corporating fuel consumption constraints in AGV systems, and intro- duced an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm. Pan et al. ( 2022 ) presented a learning-based evolutionary optimization algorithm, designing a RL-based multi-population strategy and problem-oriented local search operator. Liu et al. ( 2023 ) designed a bi-level program- ming model, constructing an integrated schedule with jobs, machines, and transportation device, and proposed an SLGA-D algorithm based on Q-learning and time windows. Cheng et al. ( 2021 ) developed a BPNN integration model based on clustering and resampling operations and proposed a dynamic weight combination strategy based on KNN for calculating completion time in FJSP-A. Yan et al. ( 2021 ) analyzed the FJSP under limited transportation resources and designed an improved genetic algorithm and a physical-Javascript object notation. Xu et al. ( 2023 ) proposed a heuristic algorithm (EHA) to solve the FJSP-A model, and designed an initialization method focused on makespan and TEC and a specific local search strategy. Li et al. ( 2020 ) investigated the FJSP-A problem with energy consumption and makespan objectives, developed several problem-specific local search operators and an im- proved Jaya algorithm. Yao et al. ( 2024b ) decomposed the FJSP-A prob- lem into four sub-decision problems and proposed a new disjunctive graph-based MILP model, with extensive instance testing demonstrat- ing the model’s superiority. 2.2. Heterogeneous AGVs and battery constraints Dang et al. ( 2021 ) investigated the scheduling of multi-load and multi-capacity AGVs with battery constraints, and considered load ca- pacity, battery thresholds, charge/discharge rates, and transportation costs of heterogeneous AGVs. Qiu et al. ( 2015 ) investigated the rout- ing problem of heterogeneous AGVs in a three-dimensional warehouse environment, and focused on the relationship between energy consump- tion and load of AGVs with different functions. Foroutan et al. ( 2020 ) considered the reverse logistics of cargo recycling and analyzed the ve- hicle routing problem for a heterogeneous fleet. Li and Huang ( 2024 ) investigated the route planning and task assignment problems of het- erogeneous AGVs with charging constraints in a logistics warehouse, and discussed the effects of the number of tasks, the number of AGVs, the maximum capacity, and the batch size on the experiment. Sabar et al. ( 2020 ) discussed the problem of fleet vehicle routing with two- dimensional loading constraints, and used heterogeneous fleets with dif- ferent capacities, operating costs, sizes, and loading constraints to serve customers. At present, the research on heterogeneous AGVs is only lim- ited to the AGV scheduling problem, and there is no research on the constraints and capabilities of heterogeneous AGVs in the FJSP-A model. 2.3. NSGA-II NSGA-II is widely applied in solving production scheduling problems due to its robustness, efficiency, and ability to handle multi-objective problems. Tao et al. ( 2024 ) designed a data-driven NSGA-II to solve the distributed flexible flow shop problem. Lim et al. ( 2022 ) constructed a three-layer planning model for cloud manufacturing service, proposed an improved NSGA-II with progressive and inheritance functions to en- hance the correlation between the three layers, and improved the coding method and population screening mechanism. sections.heading: FJSP-HA
sections.text: model In FJSP-HA, a set of jobs 𝑖 ∈{1 , 2 , … , 𝑁 } is processed on a group of machines 𝑚 ∈{1 , 2 , … , 𝑀 } . Each job 𝑖 has 𝑂 𝑖 operations. 𝑂 𝑖𝑗 denotes the 𝑗 𝑡ℎ operation of job 𝑖 . Each operation 𝑂 𝑖𝑗 can be processed by any of its optional machines, and using different machines may change the processing time and energy consumption. The transport tasks for each job are handled by a fleet of heterogeneous AGVs 𝑘 ∈{1 , 2 , … , 𝐾 } . Sim- ilarly, heterogeneous AGVs also have different speeds, energy consump- tion, battery capacities and charging speeds. The initial distribution cen- ter for the heterogeneous AGVs fleet is the load/unload area. At the start of each task, the battery level must be above a critical threshold. If an AGV’s battery level falls below this threshold during travel, it must visit a charging station after completing the current task. The charging station has sufficient space to allow multiple AGVs to charge simultaneously, ensuring no wait time. 3.1. Problem description Although processing tasks and transportation tasks are executed by machines and AGVs respectively, the start-up time of tasks on the two devices will affect and restrict each other. As shown in Fig. 1 , the FJSP- HA in this paper can be described into five interrelated parts: (1) Assign operations to suitable machines for processing. (2) Assign AGVs to each operation for transportation. (3) Determine the sequence of transporta- tion for each job. (4) Ensure adequate AGV power. (5) Determine the sequence of processing operations for each machine. The main objective of FJSP-HA is to minimize the makespan and the TEC. Within the con- straints, the system aims to optimize the performance of various AGVs, ensuring that jobs are efficiently transported to the corresponding ma- chines for processing. sections.heading: NSGA-II
sections.text: algorithm Current meta-heuristic algorithms often encounter challenges when solving multi-objective FJSP-A problems, such as insufficient solution accuracy, slow convergence, and sub-optimal solution quality. There- fore, D2NSGA-II is proposed in this paper to solve these problems. In this section, we introduce the framework of D2NSGA-II, encoding and decod- ing, initialization strategy, crossover and mutation operators, problem- driven local search operators and double DQN based local search. 4.1. Framework of D2NSGA-II The framework of D2NSGA-II is shown as Algorithm 1 , and the spe- cific steps are as follows: Firstly, the initialization strategy of a diverse population structure is used. Secondly, the crossover and mutation oper- ators are selected to generate a new population. Again, the local search operator is selected based on the trained neural network. Next, the gen- erated non-dominated neighborhood solution is retained. Then, at each generation, the first 𝑛𝑝 individuals are selected as the new population. Finally, the Pareto optimal solution is output after multiple iterations.

Encoding and decoding In this paper, the three resources to be scheduled are operations, ma- chines and AGVs, represented by using a three-layer encoding method for a feasible solution. Yan et al. ( 2021 ) used operation sequence to de- termine the order in which tasks are executed on machines and AGVs, specifically, changes in the sequence of operation affect the assignment of machines and AGVs. In particular, the problem-driven heuristic strategies, which deeply consider the problem structure and constraints, have been widely proven to significantly en- hance the algorithm convergence ( Li et al. , 2023 ; Zhang et al. , 2022 ). sections.heading: Heuristic
sections.text: 1 : A time-first heuristic 1 is proposed to generate solutions with smaller makespan. OS is generated using a random method. In the MS , the cumulative processing time record for each machine is first cal- culated. For operation 𝑂 𝑖𝑗 , the machine with the shortest cumulative processing time in the optional machine set is selected to improve load balance and machine utilization. If multiple machines have the mini- mum cumulative processing time, one is randomly chosen. In the AS , the earliest available time, transportation distance, and AGV speed of each AGV are used to calculate the earliest AGV arrival time. The AGV with the earliest arrival is selected to minimize job waiting time. Similarly, if multiple AGVs have the same earliest arrival time, one is randomly selected. These steps are repeated until all jobs are assigned to machines and AGVs.

sections.heading: Heuristic
sections.text: 2 : To address the low energy consumption requirement of the proposed model, an energy-focused heuristic is introduced. For an operation in the random OS , the processing energy consumption on al- ternative machines is calculated. The machine with the lowest energy consumption is preferred with a 50 % probability, while a random ma- chine is selected with the other 50 %, balancing low energy consumption with solution flexibility. Additionally, in the AS , the transportation dis- tance and unit energy consumption of each AGV are calculated. The AGV with the lowest energy consumption for the journey from its current po- sition to the transportation starting point is selected to minimize AGV energy consumption. This process is repeated until all jobs are assigned.

sections.text: 3 : A random method is used to generate OS , and the corre- sponding devices in MS and AS are randomly selected in their respective optional device sets, so as to maintain the diversity of population. The diversification of the initial population is generated by combin- ing the three heuristics above. Half of the initial solutions are gener- ated by heuristic 3 , while the other half are generated using heuristic 1 and heuristic 2 methods with equal probability. This diverse population structure initialization strategy helps the initial population to be closer to the optimal or high-quality solutions, thereby reducing convergence time and mitigating the risk of premature convergence. 4.4. Crossover and mutation operators In the proposed D2NSGA-II, a binary tournament mechanism is used to select two parents. Since the FJSP-HA problem involves three sub- problems, this paper proposes a different crossover mechanism for the three levels of coding. The mutation operator broadens the algorithm’s exploration of the solution space by introducing small perturbations to the solution. For the OS , a swap mutation is used, where two different jobs in the sequence are exchanged. For MS and AS , the current device used for either operation is replaced with other device in the optional device set. 4.5. sections.heading: Experimental
sections.text: analysis In this section, three parts of experiments are designed to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm and model. Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 validate the effectiveness of the improved strategy in this paper and the superiority of D2NSGA-II over other compared algorithms. Experi- ment 3 verifies the effectiveness of heterogeneous AGVs in the FJSP-HA model. All algorithms were implemented in MATLAB 2021b, running on a computer equipped with an Intel Core i9-14900K processor 3.20 GHz and 64.0 GB RAM. 5.1. Benchmarks and performance metrics We selected the benchmarks designed by Brandimarte ( 1993 ), Der- oussi and Norre ( 2010 ) respectively, and extended relevant conditions on their basis to adapt to FJSP-HA, constituting a total of 20 extended instances of eDN01-eDN10 and eMK01-eMK10. The training set was ran- domly generated and contains instances of different sizes. We use M-J- O-A to denote the size of each type of instance, where 𝑀 is the number of machines, 𝑁 is the number of jobs, 𝑂 is the number of jobs, and 𝐴 is the number of AGVs. The number of operations varies between 13 and 21 for eDN instances and between 55 and 240 for eMK instances. The job numbers are in the range {5,6,7,8,10,15,20} and the machine numbers are in the range {4,5,6,8,10,15}. Two types of heterogeneous AGVs were generated with different performances in no-load power, load power, transportation speed, battery threshold and charging rate. The AGV fleet was configured based on the number of AGVs required for each instance. All machines and AGVs are scheduled in rectangular intelligence workshop. In order to measure the actual performance of the algorithm, we use the Hypervolume (HV) and Inverse Generation Distance (IGD) ( Guer- reiro et al. , 2021 ; Ishibuchi et al. , 2015 ) as reference metrics to measure the performance of the algorithm. HV can be used to measure the per- formance in terms of convergence and diversity, with higher HV values indicating better performance. A smaller IGD value indicates that the algorithm has better overall performance. Their formulas are shown in Eqs. 24 and 25 . sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In this paper, an improved NSGA-II algorithm based on double DQN is proposed to solve the multi-objective flexible job shop scheduling problem with heterogeneous AGVs. Firstly, the mathematical model of FJSP-HA is constructed, and a population initialization strategy com- bining multiple heuristic methods is designed to improve the diversity and quality of the initial population. Secondly, the concepts of critical path and critical block in FJSP-HA are introduced. On this basis, six local search operators based on problem characteristics are designed to enhance the effectiveness of local search. Subsequently, an operator recommendation strategy based on double DQN is proposed to guide NSGA-II to select the optimal operator and improve the convergence performance of the algorithm. Through computational experiments on 20 extended instances, we find that D2NSGA-II achieves significant improvements in multiple per- formance indicators, and outperforms four comparison algorithms in all instances. Finally, we use a real world case from an auto parts supplier. The research shows that, compared with the homogeneous AGVs, the Expert Systems With Applications 296 (2026) 128992 14 R. Chen et al. heterogeneous AGVs have improved in both makespan and TEC, and the optimization effect increases with the increase in the number of processed jobs. We can conclude that heterogeneous AGVs have more potential to solve the multi-objective FJSP-A problem with battery con- straints. In future work, we will make efforts in the following aspects, in- cluding: (1) Exploring the problem properties in complex scenarios of FJSP-A problem with battery constraints to ensure the effectiveness of local search operators. (2) Investigating dynamic events in FJSP-A prob- lems to exploit the advantages of DRL in solving dynamic scheduling problems. (3) Considering the problem of partial charging of AGV, and developing a dynamic charging strategy to minimize the downtime.
